coverage_notes:
SEARCHED AND FOUND LITTLE OR NOTHING.

(1) ANCESTRY. No claim in this graph rests on a cohort with genetically inferred or self-reported ancestry as a covariate in the STK11 x immunotherapy analysis. Searches for African-ancestry, Hispanic/Latin American, and South Asian STK11-ICI cohorts returned only prevalence/driver-landscape papers and a single case report; no outcome analysis. The only ancestry-differentiated outcome evidence is indirect: a Japanese C-CAT cohort (C-023/C-024, n=343) where STK11 showed NO significant OS effect while KEAP1 did, and ORIENT-11 (Chinese) contributing to C-034/C-036. Every foundational claim (Skoulidis 2018, Ricciuti 2022, Papillon-Cavanagh 2020, Shire 2020) comes from US cohorts that do not report ancestry at all. A US clinicogenomic cohort with ancestry annotation is an open gap.

(2) SEX. No sex-stratified STK11 x immunotherapy effect estimate was found in any source. Sex appears only as an adjustment covariate (e.g. De Giglio 2025, C-026). No interaction test between sex and STK11 status was located.

(3) SMOKING STATUS. Only one claim (C-032) conditions on smoking, and it is a preclinical/correlative TMB observation in non-smokers, not an outcome analysis. No clinical cohort was found that reports STK11-ICI outcomes separately in never-smokers versus smokers, despite STK11 mutation being strongly smoking-associated. This is a first-order confounding gap.

(4) SQUAMOUS HISTOLOGY. Effectively unstudied. KEYNOTE-407 could not analyse STK11 because only 2.8% of squamous patients carried a mutation (C-022); Papillon-Cavanagh and Ricciuti both excluded squamous histology by design. Only a 2024 ASCO abstract on STK11/KEAP1/KRAS in LSCC was surfaced and it could not be retrieved (ascopubs 403). No verified squamous-specific effect estimate exists in this graph.

(5) AGE. No claim reports an age-stratified STK11 effect. No cohort reported an age range in a form that could be captured.

(6) DOSE/CLONALITY. Searches surfaced assertions that clonal vs subclonal and truncating vs missense STK11 mutations behave differently, but no primary source with an effect estimate was retrievable. No claim here distinguishes STK11 variant class, allelic status, or LOH.

(7) STK11 MUTATION VS PROTEIN/FUNCTIONAL LOSS. C-034/C-035 argue transcriptomic STK11 deficiency, not mutation, is the operative variable, but no source reporting the concordance rate between STK11 mutation and LKB1 IHC protein loss was retrieved.

(8) TEMPORAL STALENESS. The claims driving clinical practice (C-001 to C-010) rest on a 2018 cohort of n=174 with 6-7 patients per KL/KP cell in the randomized-trial component. The largest verified re-examinations are 2020-2024 (n=2276 Flatiron, n=1261 DFCI/MSK, n=4317 pooled). No verified cohort after 2022 with n>500 that reports a formal treatment-by-STK11 INTERACTION test (as opposed to a within-ICI-arm HR) was found; that is the specific design that would settle prognostic-vs-predictive and it is missing from the recent literature.

(9) FAILED RETRIEVALS. ScienceDirect, JTO, Annals of Oncology, ESMO Open, ascopubs.org and medRxiv PDF endpoints all returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch. Europe PMC and bioRxiv began returning 503/429 late in the session. Consequently: the POSEIDON 5-year primary publication (PMID 39243945) is represented only via conference reporting (C-042); C-035 carries no quote; a 2026 bioRxiv preprint on SMARCA4/STK11/KEAP1 co-inactivation and TGF-beta was located but never opened and is therefore absent; the WCLC 2019 abstract MA11.11 on STK11 and chemo-immunotherapy (reported medians 4.8 vs 7.2 months PFS, 10.6 vs 16.7 months OS) could not be opened and was NOT entered as a claim.

(10) NOT SEARCHED / OUT OF SCOPE. Non-lung tumour types, STK11 germline (Peutz-Jeghers) biology, and KRAS G12C-inhibitor monotherapy outcomes were only incidentally touched and are not represented as claims.
